correctness.rationale: Recognize lifted hubs as the unique two vertices of maximum degree when t>=2. Their pointwise stabilizer acts as S_(2k) on isolated K2 atoms and as S_r wr S_(t_r) on each family of side-identified crown components B(K_r), r>=3. A central hub-exchange involution supplies the C2 factor. The original graph automorphisms preserve the perfect matching of 2k edge atoms into k pairs, giving exact index (2k)!/(2^k k!). The t=1 complete graph is separately stable. The proof checks all hypotheses including r=2, r=3 and k=0; independent exhaustive graph automorphism enumeration matches eleven small cases but is not used to establish the general theorem.

value.rationale: The exact full symmetry group and group-index sequence for all mixed clique bouquets, together with an if-and-only-if stability criterion, identify how covering destroys a natural matching of edge atoms. This is a structurally motivated family of natural graph invariants, with unbounded extra symmetry and an invariant depending only on triangular blade count. It is not merely the known existence of instability or a single arbitrary example.
